simple.meaning: מַרְבֵּק (marbêq) is a Hebrew animal word meaning “a stall (for cattle).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at 1 Samuel 28:24. The surrounding context includes death.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַרְבֵּק (H4770) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: מַרְבֵּק (marbêq) / H4770 is traced through 1 Samuel 28:24, Jeremiah 46:21, Amos 6:4, Malachi 3:20 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H4770. marbeq מַרְבֵק noun [masculine] stall (literally tying-place ); — מ מִתּוֺךְ ׳עֲגָלִים Amos 6:4 calves out of the stall (where they were fattened); ׳עֵגֶלמֿ 1Sam 28:24 i.e. a stall-fed, fatted, calf; so מ ׳כְּעֶנְלֵי Malachi 3:20 (simile of prosperity), Jer 46:21 (simile of well-fed and arrogant mercenaries).
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root meaning to tie up ;

occurrences.englishText: The woman had a fattened calf in the house. She hurried and killed it; and she took flour, and kneaded it, and baked unleavened bread of it.
Also her hired men in the middle of her are like calves of the stall;
Who lie on beds of ivory,
